measurements.allocation: ThreadMXBean.getCurrentThreadAllocatedBytes; prepared raw values and predicate excluded from wrapper construction; read samples include the shared diagnostic Reading result record and measurement-call overhead
measurements.retained_structure: Iterative identity graph walk of M3/JDK cursor/predicate and backing ArrayList fields; original backing identity tested by reference
measurements.heap: MemoryMXBean heap used after two explicit System.gc calls; whole process observation, not an individual owner retained-byte measurement
measurements.process: POSIX wait4 CPU and peak RSS, /proc/self/status current/peak fields, HotSpot NMT summary committed/reserved bytes
measurements.samples: Three shallow warmups; seven shallow construction samples, one deep construction sample; three read warmups then seven read samples. Individual median values are diagnostic only.

resource_tradeoffs: Depth64 generic owner construction remains1560 measured bytes; traversal allocation is2112 baseline vs1056 final bytes in this run. Depth1 traversal allocation is unchanged96 bytes.

Depth64 List balanced composition increases measured construction allocation3072->10760 bytes and retains127 FilterNode objects instead of63 recursive lambda objects. It bounds recursion and preserves1088 read/128 membership callbacks.

Depth65536 generic final traversal records65536 predicate calls and854208 allocated bytes; List final traversal records131072 calls and144 allocated bytes. Both predecessors overflow on the recorded256KiB stack, so no deep throughput ratio is valid.
Depth65536 final process peak RSS was63212KiB for Collection and75424KiB for List; these include VM, observer graph walk and NMT overhead. They are not component-only memory sizes.
limits: Finite diagnostic observations do not establish statistically controlled throughput rankings or universal memory savings. No time or memory threshold is used as a correctness gate.

Small whole-process post-GC heap differences include class initialization, compilation and runtime garbage collection; negative shallow deltas are retained as observations and never interpreted as negative owner size.
NMT excludes allocations outside its tracking scope. These pure Java wrapper runs invoke no new JNI implementation and do not replace the independent JNI integration gate.
Deep membership cost is deliberately not repeated: existing depth proof and exact callback tapes retain the original quadratic visibility demand.
The first probe attempt used optional ProcessHandle.Info CPU data and was rejected when it was unavailable; its fixture/log disposition is retained separately. No product source changed.
